jobs.title: US Immigration Program Manager (Strategy & Operations)
jobs.description:
Meta is seeking an experienced U.S. Immigration Program Manager to drive the operating model and program direction for U.S. employment-based immigration, serving as a subject-matter expert on case filings and compliance operations. This role is accountable for filing quality, accuracy, and timeliness at scale, the program's U.S. compliance posture, and the frameworks, playbooks, and tooling that underpin delivery.This individual will partner closely with Recruiting, People Partners, Legal, external counsel, and business leaders to solve the most complex U.S. immigration challenges, ensure regulatory compliance, and continuously improve our case management operations. This is a senior individual contributor role operating with significant autonomy: identifying program priorities, resolving ambiguous cross-functional problems, and influencing decisions without direct authority.  
  
  

### **US Immigration Program Manager (Strategy & Operations) Responsibilities:**

* Own the design, maintenance, and continuous improvement of Meta's U.S. immigration operating model and compliance framework, including decision rights and controls for right-to-work verification, government reporting, audit readiness, and regulatory change management, in partnership with Legal, HR, and outside counsel
* Serve as a senior subject-matter expert on U.S. employment-based nonimmigrant and immigrant filings (e.g., H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN, PERM, EB-1/NIW/EB-2/EB-3, adjustment of status, and consular processing), partnering with Legal and outside counsel on case strategy, filing requirements, and adjudication trends
* Own program-level oversight of complex, high-profile, and time-sensitive immigration filings, personally leading selected escalations while scaling case preparation and execution through operational teams and outside counsel
* Develop and maintain standardized filing playbooks, templates, checklists, and quality-control protocols that enable consistent, high-quality case preparation at scale
* Monitor U.S. regulatory developments and proactively translate new requirements into updated policies, processes, and operational guidance with Legal and outside counsel
* coordinate with regional immigration leads where cases have cross-border dependencies
* Drive technology and process innovation in case management workflows: identifying opportunities for automation, AI-assisted checks with human review, and system enhancements to reduce cycle times and improve accuracy
* Act as an escalation point for complex filing scenarios, RFEs (Requests for Evidence), denials, and novel immigration questions, partnering with Legal and outside counsel on resolution paths and addressing systemic causes through process improvements
* Establish and enforce quality standards and SLAs for external immigration counsel and service providers, reviewing work product and driving accountability for filing accuracy and timeliness
* Partner cross-functionally with Legal, People Partners, Recruiting, and Finance to align U.S. immigration operations with workforce planning and talent strategy, resolve competing priorities, and clarify handoffs, with the PERM recruitment team owning recruitment execution and this role owning overall immigration case progression
* Develop compliance dashboards, reporting mechanisms, and audit processes that provide visibility into filing volumes, cycle times, compliance health, and risk exposure, and use these measures to prioritize improvements and hold teams and vendors accountable
* Set and drive a multi-quarter roadmap for the U.S. immigration program, identifying high-impact problems, making the case for investment, and sequencing initiatives against business priorities, risk, and delivery capacity with minimal management oversight

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 12+ years of progressive experience in U.S. employment-based immigration with responsibility for case filings, compliance program design, and immigration operations, including end-to-end ownership of complex programs at scale
* Deep subject-matter expertise across U.S. employment-based nonimmigrant visa categories and permanent residence pathways, including PERM, immigrant petitions, adjustment of status, and consular processing
* Demonstrated experience designing and operating U.S. immigration compliance frameworks, setting program direction, and establishing decision rights and controls across teams and external providers
* Track record of developing scalable processes, playbooks, and quality frameworks that deliver measurable improvements across multiple teams
* Experience managing relationships with external law firms and immigration vendors, including setting quality expectations and enforcing SLAs
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders (Legal, HR, Recruiting, Finance), resolve competing priorities, and drive decisions in ambiguous situations without direct authority
* Experience leveraging AI or automation tools to drive efficiency in compliance monitoring and case processing workflows

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience operating within a global technology company or a similarly complex, high-volume immigration environment
* Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
* Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
* Experience coordinating cross-border cases and partnering with regional immigration specialists outside the U.S
* Data-driven approach to measuring filing quality, cycle times, compliance health, and vendor effectiveness
* Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)

jobs.title: Automation Program Manager, Legal and Compliance Operations
jobs.description:
Legal and Compliance Operations is seeking an Automation Program Manager to help us automate high-volume review at scale across Legal and Compliance workflows. Our workflows run on a composite of LLM-based decisioning, rules-based logic that encodes policy directly, and signals drawn from reporter history, content matching and behavioral patterns. Automation now carries a substantial share of enforcement volume, which means its quality determines both the legal risk we mitigate and the experience of the rights holders, regulators and people who depend on these decisions.As an Automation Program Manager, you will own the measured quality of assigned automations. Half of the role is forward motion: taking an automation from where it performs today to where the operational plan requires, through iteration on prompts, rules and signal thresholds. The other half is regression response: when reliability, correctness, precision or recall degrades, you find out why and drive it back. An effective candidate in this role is rigorous about measurement, comfortable working across all three automation types, and able to tell a genuine regression apart from a shift in what is arriving.  
  
  

### **Automation Program Manager, Legal and Compliance Operations Responsibilities:**

* Hill-climb reliability (prompt, iterate and improve), correctness, precision and recall on assigned automations across Legal and Compliance Workflows
* Iterate on LLM components, including prompts, task decomposition, routing, and abstention and fallback behavior
* Diagnose and improve rules-based components, including coverage, ordering and precedence, conflicts between rules, rules firing on the wrong population, and rules that stop matching after a policy or schema change
* Tune signal-based components, including thresholds, signal freshness and availability, and the precision cost of upstream signal drift
* Investigate regressions to isolate whether the cause is model, rule, signal, upstream data, policy change, or a shift in the incoming population, and distinguish real degradation from volume mix shift
* Drive regressions to a measured recovery that holds across a following measurement period, and document what degraded, why it was not caught earlier, and what detection would have caught it
* Build and maintain offline eval and gold standard data sets, coordinating expert-review sampling with the reviewers who hold the ground truth
* Build regression detection that surfaces degradation before the next reporting cycle, and close measurement coverage gaps so automations that are live are also measured
* Build scripts, notebooks and internal tooling so program managers and operations leads can run measurement independently
* Document what was tried, what moved the metric, and what did not, so subsequent workflows start further along

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* 2+ years of relevant experience in data annotation, labeling, quality assurance, or content review operations, including time spent close to automated decision output
* Experience with guideline accuracy and inter-rater agreement, including diagnosing why qualified reviewers disagree
* Working knowledge of Python and SQL, with experience pulling a dataset, computing precision and recall, and segmenting results to locate where loss is concentrated
* Experience reading and reasoning about conditional logic to trace how a decision was reached
* Experience working with large operational datasets in a notebook environment
* Investigative approach to metric movement, identifying cause rather than the explanation that fits
* Experience communicating results clearly, including reporting a metric that has not moved or a regression that is not yet explained

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Experience in adversarial or fraud-adjacent domains where the reviewed population actively shifts
* Experience with rules engines, decision tables, routing logic or classifier thresholds
* Experience coordinating with vendor or cross-functional reviewer pools
* Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
* Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
* Experience or expertise in legal and compliance operations, or trust and safety
* Experience iterating on prompts with measured before-and-after results
* Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)

  
  
  

### **About Meta:**

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. management/planning and material readiness for key technologies. Responsibilities will

analysis and reporting, logistic readiness, budget, procurement, and configuration management

strategies in support of engineering development builds.  
  
**Description**  
  
Drive NPI build planning activities, which can include managing build matrices for lower-level  
  
components/assemblies, building strategic partnerships with internal and external stakeholders,  
  
developing risk mitigation plan, and executing issue resolution  
  
Manage material forecasting and planning with key module and component vendors. Drive CTB  
  
process and communicate changes to ensure clear visibility on materials lead-time, logistic readiness,  
  
and shipping plan that can meet the development builds  
  
Partner with program managers, global commodity managers and finance team to create and  
  
manage development budgets and procurement activities

part numbers, engineering change orders, and related technical drawings and documents

Supply chain management experience related to build management/planning, material clear to

jobs.title: Expert Program Manager - Clean Energy Transportation
jobs.description:
Requisition ID # 175301
  
  
**Job Category:** Project / Program Management
  
**Job Level:** Individual Contributor
  
**Business Unit:** Strategy & Growth
  
**Work Type:** Hybrid
  
**Job Location:** Oakland
  
  
Department Overview
  
The Clean Energy Transportation (CET) group is focused on accelerating the adoption of clean vehicles in California. CET leads a ~$0.5B portfolio of transportation electrification (TE) programs to increase the adoption of clean vehicles in California as we work to address one of the largest contributors to climate change – and we need a motivated, organized strategic thinker to help us determine how to expand this portfolio. We serve PG&E’s customers by deploying electric vehicle programs to increase access to charging infrastructure, reduce total cost of electric vehicle ownership, educating our customers and pursuing innovative R&D on the future of transportation electrification, focused on vehicle-grid-integration.
  
  
We focus on safety and quality, invest in our team’s success, solve problems, and strive to be better, work as an integrated team, and build trusted relationships. We collaborate and are intellectually curious. We are looking to collaborate with passionate, thoughtful people who want to make a real impact.
  
  
Position Summary
  
The CET team is looking for a highly skilled Program Manager to lead our Pre-Owned EV Rebate Program and other strategic initiatives to promote EV adoption. This will require an ability to track and manage all budget and regulatory requirements, provide direct support to customers, and creatively problem solve. It will also require collaboration with other internal teams and engaging with external parties, like investor-owned utilities (IOUs).
  
  
**Specific areas of responsibility for this role will include:** Overseeing the day-to-day implementation of the program including ongoing operational tasks, technical elements, regulatory requirements, customer and external stakeholder engagement, budget monitoring, and metrics reporting. Responsible for driving best practices/efficiencies related to delivering on program goals. Managing contracts to confirm goals are met and the program stays within budget.
  
  
In addition to program management, specific areas of regulatory compliance include reporting to the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) or the California Air Resources Board (CARB.)
  
  
The successful candidate will have a strong background in program, product and/or project management with experience operating in a regulated environment under the jurisdiction of the CPUC or CARB, identifying and collaborating with key internal and external stakeholders to formulate ideas, develop well-reasoned solutions, and resolve issues will be essential to the position. The candidate will have excellent critical thinking, analytical, and communication skills while demonstrating knowledge of and attention to details. Experience with transportation electrification and electric vehicles is highly desired.
  
  
This position is hybrid, working from your remote office and your assigned work location based on business need. The preferred work location is Oakland, CA.
  
  
PG&E is providing the full salary/pay range for this position. The actual amount paid to an individual will be based on multiple factors, including, but not limited to, internal equity, specific skills, education, licenses or certifications, experience, market value, and geographic location. The range to reasonably expect will be between the minimum and the midpoint of the range. The final decision will be made on a case-by-case basis related to the factors above. This job is also eligible to participate in PG&E’s discretionary incentive compensation programs.

**Bay Area Midpoint:** $168,000.00
  
**Bay Area Maximum:** $207,000.00

**Minimum Qualifications:** Bachelor degree or equivalent experience 8 years of experience
  
  
**Desired Qualifications:** Advanced knowledge of Program Management Excellent communication skills are required – i.e. the ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and effectively both orally and in written documents Interest, willingness, and aptitude to learn new subjects related to Transportation Electrification Strong analytic skills and the ability to solve complex problems Demonstrated experience improving processes Sound understanding of administering rebate and incentive programs Proven track record for developing and maintaining program budgets, long-term forecasts, and performing day-to-day tasks, like approving vendor invoices and managing ongoing accruals Experience implementing CARB Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS) regulations Detail oriented with excellent organization, prioritization, and time management skills Experience in a regulated environment

jobs.title: Client Care Manager
jobs.description:
**Why GoldLeaf?**
-----------------

We're a woman-owned, locally rooted home care agency serving families across the Peninsula and South Bay. We grew through word of mouth, one family at a time and we continue to grow.

We support older adults, people living with dementia, and adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. Our goal is to help each of them live safely, comfortably, and with dignity at home.

As a rapidly expanding organization and our continuous momentum, you'll have significant opportunities to grow your career and evolve alongside us. If you want work where you can see the difference you make every day, we'd love to meet you.

**About the Role**
------------------

As our Client Care Manager, you'll be the heart of the care experience. You'll be the person families call first, the one caregivers trust, and the one who makes sure every client gets the right care from the right caregiver.

You'll guide each client's journey from the first phone call through ongoing care. That means assessing needs in the home, building personalized care plans, matching caregivers thoughtfully, and checking in often so small concerns never become big ones. You'll also help build and support our caregiver team: recruiting, onboarding, coaching, scheduling and recognizing the people who make our care possible.

You'll lead our caregiver team and client care operations. That means overseeing care plans, supervising and developing our caregivers, and owning the client and family experience from start to finish. The role combines time in our Mountain View office with regular client home visits, plus leading our on-call coverage every other weekend.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

### **Client care and assessments**

* Conduct warm, thorough intake calls and in-home assessments to understand each client's physical, cognitive, emotional, and safety needs, along with their routines and preferences.
* Create, update, and maintain personalized care plans that reflect each client's goals and changing conditions.
* Serve as the main point of contact for clients and families. Give regular updates, answer questions, and help families understand how changes in condition affect care needs.
* Spot changes early and escalate concerns appropriately, including coordinating with families, caregivers, and other providers when needed.
* Complete supervisory and quality-assurance home visits and home safety checks to confirm care is safe, consistent, and meets GoldLeaf standards.

### **Leading the caregiver team**

* Supervise and direct our team of caregivers, including setting expectations, coaching performance, and recognizing great work.
* Make hiring, discipline, and termination decisions and recommendations in partnership with the owner.
* Oversee caregiver scheduling and client matching. You'll make the final call on the right caregiver for each client and resolve coverage gaps.

**Location:** This is a fully remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office).

**Type:** This is a full-time position

  

**About the Team**

The Data Science team develops analytical approaches, statistical models, and machine learning capabilities that help College Board make better decisions and deliver stronger outcomes for students and educators. Our growing team partners across research, product, engineering, business intelligence, and operations to turn complex questions and data into useful, responsible, and scalable solutions. This role supports both Data Science Core and Gen AI Studio teams.

  

The work spans exploratory analysis, experimentation, model development, production delivery, and ongoing monitoring. Accuracy, transparency, privacy, and responsible use of data are essential, particularly in high-stakes education contexts. What makes this team distinctive is its combination of rigorous data science, practical problem-solving, and sustained cross-functional collaboration.

As Program Manager, Data Science, you will create the structure and operating discipline that enables a growing data science portfolio to deliver meaningful results. You will connect strategy to execution by managing roadmaps, priorities, dependencies, risks, decision points, and communication across multiple workstreams. A core part of this work is making sure projects are ready before Data Science delivery begins: prerequisites confirmed, dependencies explicit, and decisions made on time.

  

You will partner closely with data scientists, data and software engineers, product managers, researchers, and business leaders. You will help teams translate ambiguous goals into executable plans, maintain momentum through changing conditions, and make tradeoffs visible. You are not expected to serve as the lead data scientist; you will bring enough technical fluency to understand the data science lifecycle, ask sharp questions, and help specialists do their best work.

Success in this role will be measured by the team's ability to focus on the highest-value work, deliver reliable outcomes predictably, manage risk early, and build trust with partners.

* Track program health and outcomes using meaningful measures rather than activity alone, and use evidence to improve plans and processes.
Maintain clear program artifacts, including roadmaps, dependency maps, decision logs, risk registers, and executive-ready updates.  

**Orchestrate Cross Functional Execution (25%)**

* Coordinate work across data science, research, product, engineering, analytics, privacy, legal, security, and business teams.
* Build executable plans from ambiguous goals and align contributors on scope, responsibilities, milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
* Facilitate decisions and resolve blockers without replacing the judgment of technical or domain experts.

**Build Stakeholder Alignment and Adoption (15%)**

* Communicate complex data science work in clear language appropriate to the audience, including uncertainty, model limitations, and responsible-use considerations.

Run the agency so the founder can build it.

You'll get the keys to how the agency runs: people, process, capacity and the money side of ops. You'll also get a founder who actually wants to let go of them.

One 10 Media isn't just another eCommerce growth agency. We run Meta and Google Ads and Klaviyo email and SMS retention for DTC brands. We're a top Klaviyo partner. We're a fully remote team of 10+ who have been working together for several years. We genuinely care about the work, the results, and each other. We're proactive, we say the thing even when it's uncomfortable, and we work with no egos and no silos.

**The Role**

You'll run day-to-day operations and report directly to our Founder & CEO, which frees him to focus on growth. This is a real ownership seat, not an assistant role. You set the rhythm, make the calls, and build the systems that let a small agency scale without breaking. The seat can grow into Director of Operations as we grow.

Full-time, remote (US) on Eastern business hours.

**What You'll Own**

* People and policies: team policies, PTO and time off approvals and coverage, and the team policy book.

* Capacity and resourcing: who's working on what, workload across client pods, and when we need to hire.

* Process: our SOPs and Asana setup, working with our SOP/QA coordinator so everything has an owner and a due date.

new_jobs.title: Client Care Manager
new_jobs.description:
**Why GoldLeaf?**
-----------------

We're a woman-owned, locally rooted home care agency serving families across the Peninsula and South Bay. We grew through word of mouth, one family at a time and we continue to grow.

We support older adults, people living with dementia, and adults with developmental and intellectual disabilities. Our goal is to help each of them live safely, comfortably, and with dignity at home.

As a rapidly expanding organization and our continuous momentum, you'll have significant opportunities to grow your career and evolve alongside us. If you want work where you can see the difference you make every day, we'd love to meet you.

**About the Role**
------------------

As our Client Care Manager, you'll be the heart of the care experience. You'll be the person families call first, the one caregivers trust, and the one who makes sure every client gets the right care from the right caregiver.

You'll guide each client's journey from the first phone call through ongoing care. That means assessing needs in the home, building personalized care plans, matching caregivers thoughtfully, and checking in often so small concerns never become big ones. You'll also help build and support our caregiver team: recruiting, onboarding, coaching, scheduling and recognizing the people who make our care possible.

You'll lead our caregiver team and client care operations. That means overseeing care plans, supervising and developing our caregivers, and owning the client and family experience from start to finish. The role combines time in our Mountain View office with regular client home visits, plus leading our on-call coverage every other weekend.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

### **Client care and assessments**

* Conduct warm, thorough intake calls and in-home assessments to understand each client's physical, cognitive, emotional, and safety needs, along with their routines and preferences.
* Create, update, and maintain personalized care plans that reflect each client's goals and changing conditions.
* Serve as the main point of contact for clients and families. Give regular updates, answer questions, and help families understand how changes in condition affect care needs.
* Spot changes early and escalate concerns appropriately, including coordinating with families, caregivers, and other providers when needed.
* Complete supervisory and quality-assurance home visits and home safety checks to confirm care is safe, consistent, and meets GoldLeaf standards.

### **Leading the caregiver team**

* Supervise and direct our team of caregivers, including setting expectations, coaching performance, and recognizing great work.
* Make hiring, discipline, and termination decisions and recommendations in partnership with the owner.
* Oversee caregiver scheduling and client matching. You'll make the final call on the right caregiver for each client and resolve coverage gaps.
* Review and approve caregiver timesheets and EVV records before payroll.

### **Recruiting and developing caregivers**

* Lead caregiver recruiting: interview, screen, and select new caregivers, and give every candidate a positive experience.
* Lead caregiver orientations, client-specific introductions, and in-service trainings.
* Run caregiver performance reviews and decide on recognition, counseling, and corrective action in line with GoldLeaf policy.
* Make sure personnel files for all caregivers stay complete and current.

### **Client satisfaction and growth**

* Run our client satisfaction check-ins, follow up on concerns, and turn feedback into better care.
* Listen to, investigate, and resolve client and family concerns with patience and care.
* Build relationships with referral partners such as hospitals, rehab centers, senior living communities, and regional centers, and help with community outreach.
* Connect families with helpful community resources.

### **Documentation and compliance**

* Keep accurate, timely records of assessments, care plans, visit notes, incidents, and client communications in our care management system.
* Follow California Home Care Services Bureau requirements, agency policies, and privacy standards.

### **On-call**

* Lead after-hours on-call coverage **every other weekend**. You'll handle caregiver call-offs, family questions, and urgent client needs. Weekend on-call is included in your salary but we’ll accommodate time off during the week when on-call duty is significant.

------------------------------

* Have **3+ years of experience** in care coordination, case management, or client services, including at least 3 year supervising or leading staff, ideally in home care, home health, hospice, assisted living, or a disability services setting.
* Truly enjoy older adults, people living with dementia, and adults with developmental or intellectual disabilities, and treat every person with dignity.
* Stay calm and clear-headed when things change quickly.
* Communicate warmly and clearly, by phone, in person, and in writing, with families, caregivers, and healthcare partners.
* Are highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable juggling many priorities.
* Have good judgment and can work independently while knowing when to ask for help.

* Dementia care training or experience with regional center clients.
* Familiarity with common medical terminology.

**College Board - Technology - Data Science Core & GenAI Studio**

**Location:** This is a fully remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office).

**Type:** This is a full-time position

  

**About the Team**

The Data Science team develops analytical approaches, statistical models, and machine learning capabilities that help College Board make better decisions and deliver stronger outcomes for students and educators. Our growing team partners across research, product, engineering, business intelligence, and operations to turn complex questions and data into useful, responsible, and scalable solutions. This role supports both Data Science Core and Gen AI Studio teams.

  

The work spans exploratory analysis, experimentation, model development, production delivery, and ongoing monitoring. Accuracy, transparency, privacy, and responsible use of data are essential, particularly in high-stakes education contexts. What makes this team distinctive is its combination of rigorous data science, practical problem-solving, and sustained cross-functional collaboration.

  

**About the Opportunity**

As Program Manager, Data Science, you will create the structure and operating discipline that enables a growing data science portfolio to deliver meaningful results. You will connect strategy to execution by managing roadmaps, priorities, dependencies, risks, decision points, and communication across multiple workstreams. A core part of this work is making sure projects are ready before Data Science delivery begins: prerequisites confirmed, dependencies explicit, and decisions made on time.

  

You will partner closely with data scientists, data and software engineers, product managers, researchers, and business leaders. You will help teams translate ambiguous goals into executable plans, maintain momentum through changing conditions, and make tradeoffs visible. You are not expected to serve as the lead data scientist; you will bring enough technical fluency to understand the data science lifecycle, ask sharp questions, and help specialists do their best work.

Success in this role will be measured by the team's ability to focus on the highest-value work, deliver reliable outcomes predictably, manage risk early, and build trust with partners.

  

**In this role you will**

* Track program health and outcomes using meaningful measures rather than activity alone, and use evidence to improve plans and processes.
Maintain clear program artifacts, including roadmaps, dependency maps, decision logs, risk registers, and executive-ready updates.  

**Orchestrate Cross Functional Execution (25%)**

* Coordinate work across data science, research, product, engineering, analytics, privacy, legal, security, and business teams.
* Build executable plans from ambiguous goals and align contributors on scope, responsibilities, milestones, dependencies, and acceptance criteria.
* Facilitate decisions and resolve blockers without replacing the judgment of technical or domain experts.
Manage handoffs from research and prototyping through production delivery, adoption, and operational ownership.  

  

**Drive Program Strategy and Portfolio Planning (20%)**

* Translate Data Science strategy and business priorities into a clear portfolio of programs, workstreams, milestones, and measurable outcomes.

* Lead intake and prioritization in partnership with Data Science leaders, balancing impact, effort, capacity, risk, and sequencing.
* Establish readiness criteria so projects have confirmed prerequisites, including data access, legal and privacy review, a named business owner, and agreed success measures, before Data Science delivery begins.
Define program success measures and establish clear ownership, decision rights, and escalation paths.  

  

**Build Stakeholder Alignment and Adoption (15%)**

* Serve as a trusted partner to technical and non-technical leaders, creating shared understanding of objectives, constraints, tradeoffs, and progress.
* Communicate complex data science work in clear language appropriate to the audience, including uncertainty, model limitations, and responsible-use considerations.
* Create feedback loops with users and stakeholders so that solutions address real needs and adoption is planned from the beginning.
Prepare concise recommendations and decision materials that help leaders act with the right context.  

  

**Strengthen Team Effectiveness and Scale (10%)**

* Protect focus by reducing avoidable interruptions, clarifying priorities, and improving how work enters and moves through the team.
* Promote documentation, reuse, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement across programs.
